newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia criticises Israel settlers benefits.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia criticises Israel settlers benefits.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said Israel's decision to grant financial benefits to Jewish settlers consolidated its occupation of Arab land and violated peace agreements, the official Saudi Press Agency reported.
It said the Saudi cabinet, in a statement after a weekly meeting on Monday night, "criticised Israel's decision to encourage the building of more Jewish settlements".
It said the kingdom "sees this decision as going back on agreements between the Palestinian Authority and Israel and a continued consolidation of Israel's occupation of Arab land".
It said King Fahd lauded the stand of the United States, a close Saudi ally, on the issue of settlements.

Israel and the Palestinians resumed talks in the last two days on a self-rule accord for the town of Hebron -- prodded by U.S. President Bill Clinton who insisted the time had come for a deal -- ending a 10-day break marked by shootings and tensions over Jewish settlements.
Under a 1995 deal between Israel and the Palestinians, Israel is supposed to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

A White House spokesman said on Monday that Washington found the latest Israeli policy on settlements "a complicating factor" in efforts to reach peace. Clinton, asked if he would call West Bank settlements an obstacle to peace, said: "Absolutely".
